subject: Notice: Regional routing failover activated — impacts to hosted inference (US-WEST-1)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Nadia Morales <nadia.morales@archipelagohealth.com>, Archipelago Health Support <support@archipelagohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: Regional routing failover activated — impacts to hosted inference (US-WEST-1)

Hello Nadia / Archipelago team,

I wanted to notify you directly that at 09:05 PDT today we detected elevated 5xx rates and prolonged p95 latency for hosted inference requests routed to our US-West-1 pool. To protect latency-sensitive flows we triggered a regional routing failover: affected traffic was rerouted to our US-East and US-Central pools with automatic model variant fallback.

Impact summary:
- Window: ~09:05–09:40 PDT (in-progress for some customers at time of note)
- Observed: short-lived 5xx spike (peak ~1.3% of requests), p95 increase to ~3.1s for some endpoints before failover
- Customer-visible: higher error rates for a subset of sessions and a transient increase in latency for routed requests

What we did immediately:
- Activated routing failover to reduce error surface and preserve throughput for production traffic
- Brought up additional capacity in US-Central and adjusted KV cache warmup to reduce cold-start latency
- Published an incident on our status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/USW1-2026-08-01-12345

What to expect next:
- We'll keep the failover in place while we complete triage (estimated 4–8 hours for initial root-cause hypothesis)
- We'll share a follow-up update in this thread and on the status page with RCA and mitigation steps

Immediate ask for you: if you see sustained errors or traffic patterns caused by this routing change (e.g., session affinity issues or truncated streaming segments), reply with the request ids or example timestamps and we'll prioritize those for replay.

Attachments: ops_incident_slack_export.txt (ops timeline snapshot)

Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as high priority. I'll loop in our SRE lead and keep you updated.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Nadia Morales <nadia.morales@archipelagohealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: Regional routing failover activated — impacts to hosted inference (US-WEST-1)

Thanks Sean — appreciate the heads up. We started seeing increased 500/502 responses in our logs around 09:10 PDT; a handful of our long-running conversational sessions were truncated and a few webhook retries piled up.

I'll pull some example request ids and send them shortly. Two quick questions:
1) Is there any expected change to token accounting/billing for the rerouted requests?
2) Do you anticipate any durability or session-loss risk from the KV cache warmup you mentioned?

We rely on low-latency responses for our triage workflow, so any ETA on full restoration would help our on-call routing.

—Nadia
Nadia Morales
Head of Platform Engineering, Archipelago Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Nadia Morales <nadia.morales@archipelagohealth.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2026 10:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: Regional routing failover activated — impacts to hosted inference (US-WEST-1)

Sean — quick update from ops and a short mitigation plan.

Triage notes (so far):
- Root signal: an autoscaling miscoordination during a kernel rollout caused a brief period where several inference workers returned transient 502s while reconnecting to their quantized kernels. The control-plane rollout started 08:58 PDT; errors surfaced 09:05–09:18 PDT.
- Failover rationale: routing to other pools prevented broader SLO violations; we also disabled the rollout to avoid repeat impact.

Mitigation actions taken:
- Rollout paused and kernel configuration rolled back to the last verified release (v2.3.7)
- Targeted cache prewarm for high-traffic customer keyspaces (this may cause slightly higher p95 for warmed sessions until warmup completes)
- Expanded capacity in US-Central by +20% as a temporary headroom buffer

Answering Nadia's questions:
1) Token accounting/billing: rerouted requests are billed normally; we are evaluating whether to apply a goodwill credit for impacted request windows and will coordinate with finance.
2) KV cache warmup: short-lived risk of slightly elevated latency; session state durability is not expected to be lost — we will monitor for any cache-miss cascades and notify if we see related errors.

Attaching ops timeline snapshot for reference: ops_incident_slack_export.txt

Suggest we send a concise customer follow-up in ~60–90 minutes with a clearer ETA once kernel rollback metrics stabilize.

- Marissa
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Nadia Morales <nadia.morales@archipelagohealth.com>, Archipelago Health Support <support@archipelagohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Update: failover status and estimated restoration window

Hi Nadia — quick update following the rollback and stabilization tests.

Status: kernel rollout was paused and rolled back at ~09:30 PDT; error rates have returned to baseline (~0.05% 5xx) for most customers. We are keeping the routing failover active for a short stabilization window while we validate model-serving telemetry across warm caches.

Estimated next steps / ETA:
- 11:45–13:00 PDT: metrics validation and gradual re-introduction of live routing for low-risk traffic (no change to your existing traffic unless we confirm stability)
- If validation looks clean, we expect to return traffic to US-West-1 by ~13:15 PDT; if anomalies persist we'll extend the failover and provide a second update.

Billing: as Marissa noted, standard usage billing applies. We'll follow up on any discretionary credits after RCA.

If you can share the example request ids and timestamps, we will prioritize replays and map them to the ops timeline. Thank you for the quick heads up — this helped prioritize your keyspace in the prewarm.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Nadia Morales <nadia.morales@archipelagohealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Final: post-incident follow-up and link to postmortem

Hi Nadia — thanks again for your patience. We're closing the incident and publishing the post-incident summary. Key points:

RCA (concise):
- A kernel rollout to inference workers in US-West-1 misapplied a compatibility flag for a subset of quantized kernels, causing transient 502s while affected workers reinitialized their state. The control-plane rollout and host-level autoscaling were both factors in the blast radius.

Remediations completed:
- Rollback to v2.3.7 and temporary block on automated kernel rollouts until additional preflight checks are in place
- Control-plane rollout gating added for kernel changes to prevent simultaneous worker restarts across availability zones
- Increased canary sampling and added a short delay between kernel activation and autoscaler triggers

Customer next steps offered:
- We published the postmortem draft (link below) and will schedule a 30-minute sync if you'd like us to walk through the timeline and impact on your traffic.
- As a goodwill gesture we will issue a one-time credit covering the window 09:05–09:40 PDT; our finance team will coordinate separately.

Postmortem link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aB2cDEF-postmortem-archipelago
Attachments: postmortem-draft-aug01.pdf, archipelago_mutual_action_plan.pdf

If you'd like a call, propose a few times and we'll book an engineering + account lead.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
VP, Customer Success & Reliability
Redwood Inference
